html:
The Shalamar Gardens are a Mughal garden on the edge of Lahore, Pakistan, built for the emperor Shah Jahan in 1641 and 1642.

They follow the Persian charbagh plan, a walled garden divided by water channels into parts, laid out on three terraces that step down. A canal brought water from far upstream to feed over 400 fountains, marble pools and waterfalls, which cooled the air in the Punjab summer. Pavilions of brick and marble let the court rest by the water.

The gardens were damaged and stripped of marble in the 18th century, but restored under Ranjit Singh and later the British. Together with the Lahore Fort, near the Badshahi Mosque, they became a World Heritage Site in 1981. They are among the best kept examples of the Mughal love of gardens begun by Babur.
sum: The Shalamar Gardens are a Mughal garden on the edge of Lahore, Pakistan, built for the emperor Shah Jahan in 1641 and 1642.
